title: security: rbac v2 - enforce KMS residency + audit logging hardening
author: Arielle Chen
description: Context: This PR tightens RBAC v2 enforcement around KMS key residency and audit logging to meet upcoming compliance requirements (EU data residency and customer-managed KMS constraints). Motivation: several customers requested stronger guarantees that keys and key usage events cannot be routed outside their designated regions, and our internal compliance review flagged gaps in how KMS region pinning and audit-forwarding interact with RBAC policies. What this PR does: - Adds a region-residency enforcement layer for KMS operations in the RBAC v2 policy evaluator. Policy decisions now consider a new 'kms_residency' claim on resources and deny key usage when residency constraints are violated. - Extends audit logging to include KMS key usage metadata (key id, requested region, resolved region, policy decision id) and surfaces these events to the audit-forwarder pipeline with a new minimal schema. - Adds a fail-safe policy: when audit-forwarding to a configured customer audit sink is unavailable, KMS operations that require audited logging are denied instead of retroactively logged. This is opt-in via feature flag for existing customers to allow staged rollout. - Hardens KMS-related policy unit tests and adds an integration test to simulate cross-region fallback behavior. - Updates docs and Linear tickets. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of kms_residency checks in rbac evaluator - [x] Audit event schema and forwarder hook - [x] Feature flag for strict-audit-fail-blocking - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and migration notes (release notes) Related: ENG-1983 (policy work), SEC-721 (compliance request), SUP-4421 (customer incident that motivated hotfix). Rollout plan: feature rolled behind feature flag; enable for internal staging for 48h, then opt-in customers, then gradual enforcement for all customers after monitoring. Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/ENG-1983-kms-residency-design, compliance notes: https://linear.app/redwood/SEC-721.
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial evaluator changes (kms_residency claim), audit-event schema, opt-in feature flag, unit tests, integration test harness, docs and migration notes.
review_comments: Marcus Rivera: Please double-check the policy evaluation ordering; I saw a potential short-circuit that could skip residency checks when a preceding allow rule matches. Requesting a small refactor.
Arielle Chen (author): Addressed — reordered evaluator rule application and added explicit residency pre-check. New unit tests added covering short-circuit cases.
Priya Nair: Can we include the KMS key alias in the audit event? It helps customer mapping. Also request that we redact account IDs in forwarded events.
Arielle Chen (author): Included alias and redaction logic in kms_event_v1 schema; forwarder masks account ids before emission. Added unit tests for redaction.
Luca Moretti: Integration test looks good, but e2e failed once in CI due to timing on forwarder start; added retry logic in test harness.
Arielle Chen (author): Added exponential backoff to test harness and CI retry documented.
release_notes: Security: RBAC v2 KMS residency enforcement and audit logging hardening. Adds KMS residency checks to policy evaluation, expands audit events to include KMS metadata, and adds an opt-in strict-audit fail-safe. Rollout behind feature flag; see docs for migration steps.
notes: This change is behind a feature flag and requires ops to update audit-forwarder sink configuration for customers with custom sinks. Coordinate with oncall and compliance before broad enforcement.
migration_instructions: 1) Run migration 20260210_kms_residency (adds config schema and default flags). 2) Enable feature flag for staging via admin console. 3) Verify audit-forwarder connectivity and downstream consumer redaction. 4) Gradually enable for opt-in customers, monitor metrics: audit_forwarder_retries, kms_policy_denials.

qa_notes: Added unit and integration tests. QA should validate: cross-region key usage denied when kms_residency mismatch, audit events include key alias and redacted account ids, forwarder behavior when sink is down results in denied KMS operations when strict-audit feature is enabled.
auditing_impact: Audit events now include: key_id, key_alias, requested_region, resolved_region, policy_decision_id. Events are sent to the same forwarder topic and follow existing retention and redaction policies.
